name: IN FULL BLOOM
notes: $1000 'fragrant purple spring blossoms / pale shade' fit lavender as well as lilac (two-answer clue); anchored with NH's state flower (web-verified purple lilac, 1919) and re-scored 48; other four rows all check out.

name: HOMEGROWN
notes: Tomato-is-a-fruit, Bugs's carrot (eyesight claim properly hedged 'is said to be'), zucchini surplus lore, toxic rhubarb leaves, wait-years asparagus wisdom all correct; gentle clean ladder.

name: BACKYARD BIRDS
notes: Cardinal as state bird of exactly 7 states web-verified (IL IN KY NC OH VA WV); chickadee-says-its-name and Toronto Blue Jays hooks land; very winnable for the demographic.

name: SUPPER'S READY
notes: Meatloaf, mac & cheese, pot roast, chicken and dumplings all solid; shepherd's pie correctly specifies lamb (beef would be cottage pie); warm comfort-food ladder.

name: BAKING DAY
notes: Toll House Inn origin, yeast as single-celled leavener, banana bread, lemon-meringue all accurate; rows 1-2 nearly flat in difficulty but both trivially gentle, fine for Easy Breezy.

name: SO THE SAYING GOES
notes: Five real proverbs (early bird/worm, chickens, glass houses/stones, watched pot, necessity/invention), each with one unambiguous completion; ideal register for older players.

name: COUNTRY WISDOM
notes: All folklore properly hedged ('supposedly', 'old-timers insist', 'folklore says'); groundhog, May flowers, lightning, red-sky sailors, cows-lie-down-rain all standard lore; charming set.

name: THE SEWING BASKET
notes: Thimble, tomato pincushion, hem, Isaac Singer wordplay (no leak), darning egg all correct; the Singer row is the standout clue of the file.

name: HANDMADE WITH LOVE
notes: $200 quilt clue contained 'patchwork' and 'batting' -- both literal answers in sibling e2 PIECE BY PIECE (round 1 would prime round 2); reworded without the leak words and re-scored 47; crochet 'little hook' etymology and macrame row correct.

name: SUNDAY MORNING
notes: Choir loft, steeple hand-rhyme, collection plate, potluck, and John Newton/'Amazing Grace' (ex-slave-ship captain, 'wretch... once was lost') all accurate; no dup with e2's hymn category.

name: BEING NEIGHBORLY
notes: Lemonade stand, welcome casserole, bake sale, Amish barn raising all solid; Welcome Wagon founded 1928 web-verified (Thomas Briggs, Memphis).

name: HOUSEHOLD HINTS
notes: Baking soda in fridge, vinegar windows, blue-and-yellow WD-40 can, mothballs vs wool-moth larvae, 'elbow grease' slang all correct; brand answers add nice variety.
